Instituts 1899, p. 287: "Everywhere, along with the principled equalization, the preservation of the old forms and names goes hand in hand: the January New Year and the Roman month names remain absent from the East, but the principles of the fixed solar year and the leap day are uniformly implemented."

summary.headline: Dog Star, Arcturus, and Month Equivalences
summary.text: Discussion of stellar calendar dates in the greater dodecaeteris, including the rising of the Dog Star and setting of Arcturus, with comparisons among Roman, Alexandrian, and other authorities. The text then explains the Syromacedonian year and aligns Augustan month names such as Sebastos, Agrippaios, Libaios, Oktaouaios, Neronaios, Anchisaios, and Romaios with Roman months.
